items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Business logic uses cryptic single-letter names: `g`, `d`, `a`, `M`, `k`, `st`, `lab`, `cen`, `bw`, `aj`. Of the three main functions, only `analyze()` has a comment, and that is inline. None has a docstring. The module docstring and the named constants (HURDLE_X, AIR_MARGIN) help, but the single-letter cap applies.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The split between read_gray_frames, analyze and find_jump matches the convention, and there are no imshow calls or frame dumps. However, `analyze` (~45 lines) and `find_jump` (~55 lines) are both long, and tuning values are inlined: `area > 800`, `aj < 40`, `+ 60`, `percentile(ref, 85)`, `(9, 9)` kernel.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: There is no `cap.isOpened()` check, though an empty frame list does exit with a message. Many tuning numbers are hard-coded rather than named (800, 40, 60, 85). Weak detections fall back to placeholder values instead of an error: `return 0, n - 1`, and `cross±1` when no airborne run is found.

items.name: Robust to bad inputs and missing detections
items.name_zh: 异常输入与检测失败的处理
items.evidence: When fewer than 3 frames show the runner, `find_jump` silently returns `0, n - 1`. When no airborne run is found it returns `cross-1, cross+1`. Both cases write made-up frames instead of exiting non-zero. There is no isOpened() check, and HURDLE_X=530 and DIFF_THRESH=30 are absolute values fitted to the one example video.

items.name: Output contract honoured
items.evidence: Input path comes from `sys.argv[1]`, and output defaults to `/app/output.toml`. The file contains exactly `jump_takeoff_frame_number` and `jump_land_frame_number`, both cast with `int(...)`. The agent stated the 0-based frame numbering in its final message.
